findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 for External Audit plan Addendum
findings.headline: Fraud policy remains non-compliant with Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023 (effective 1 September 2025)
findings.detail: The auditor recommends the council review and update its fraud policy to comply with the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023, which became effective on 1 September 2025. The council is now operating 11 months past the compliance deadline without reported remediation.
findings.matters: The Act creates personal liability for senior management and organisations that fail to prevent fraud. Operating non-compliant with a statutory requirement is a governance red flag and exposes the council to Serious Fraud Office enforcement action.
findings.figures: Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023 effective 1 September 2025; compliance deadline now 11 months overdue
findings.quote: The Council needs to review its fraud policy and ensure it is compliant with the new Act to mitigate the risk of enforcement action

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 for External Audit plan Addendum
findings.headline: 2024/25 Outturn Report omitted analysis of savings delivered versus savings planned, preventing verification of budget management effectiveness
findings.detail: The auditor identified that the 2024/25 Outturn Report did not analyse how much of the council's planned savings were actually achieved, preventing members and external users from verifying whether the council is capable of executing its financial improvement plans.
findings.matters: Lenders assess creditworthiness on whether a council can deliver planned savings and manage expenditure. Absence of savings reporting prevents assessment of management's capability to execute financial plans or whether planned improvements are real.
findings.figures: 2024/25 Outturn Report savings achievement analysis missing
findings.quote: The 2024/25 Outturn Report did not include an analysis of the savings achieved against the planned level. This makes it difficult for members to hold officers to account if savings are not achieved.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 for External Audit plan Addendum
findings.headline: Delays in subsidiary (Seven Arches Investment Limited) audit prevented group consolidation working papers
findings.detail: The council's wholly-owned investment subsidiary, Seven Arches Investment Limited (SAIL), experienced audit delays that prevented the council from providing working papers to support the 2024/25 group audit. SAIL holds £56.73 million of investment properties which consolidate into group accounts.
findings.matters: Group accounts must consolidate all material subsidiaries. Delays in component audits cascade to delay group reporting. Investment property valuations in SAIL may be pledged as security or relevant to covenant compliance, making timely audit assurance essential.
findings.figures: SAIL investment properties £56.73 million; group audit procedures not completed due to subsidiary audit delays
findings.quote: Due to delays experienced in the subsidiary audit, management were unable to provide relevant financial working papers to support the execution of required audit procedures for the 2024/25 audit.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 for External Audit plan Addendum
findings.headline: Draft 2024/25 financial statements contained material misstatement that internal quality review failed to detect
findings.detail: The auditor identified a material misstatement to PPE in the draft financial statements, along with multiple non-material errors (inconsistencies, typographical and arithmetic errors) that should have been caught before submission for audit. This indicates the council's finance team lacks resource or capability to produce error-free first-draft accounts.
findings.matters: If the council cannot produce materially accurate draft financial statements, it suggests insufficient finance team capacity, lack of expertise, or weak transaction controls. Material errors in PPE specifically raise questions about asset tracking and valuation governance.
findings.figures: One material misstatement to PPE; multiple non-material internal inconsistencies, typographical and arithmetic errors in draft statements
findings.quote: There number of non-material internal inconsistencies, typographical and arithmetic errors in the draft financial statements that should have been detected through internal quality review prior to publication. One of these was a material misstatement to PPE.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 for External Audit plan Addendum
findings.headline: Minimum Revenue Provision (MRP) calculation not audited for five years; prior fraud risk never resolved
findings.detail: The council's MRP—the annual charge for repaying loans—has not been audited since 2020/21 when a fraud risk was identified due to the council's increased leverage and high degree of judgement in the calculation. Prior errors were proposed in 2020/21 but assurance has not been updated since.
findings.matters: MRP directly determines the council's prudential borrowing headroom and annual debt servicing cost. Errors or manipulation here affect both the council's ability to borrow and its stated financial forecasts. A fraud risk unreviewed for five years represents a control gap.
findings.figures: MRP not audited since 2020/21; fraud risk identified in 2020/21 due to Council's increase in financing and level of judgement in calculation
findings.quote: As we have not audited this balance since 2020/21, we have identified this as an inherent risk for 2025/26 (as we did in 2024/25) and will undertake procedures to assess whether MRP is materially accurate in the accounts and calculated in line with Statutory requirements.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 for External Audit plan Addendum
findings.headline: Opening reserve balances for 2025/26 cannot be quantified due to gaps in prior year audit coverage
findings.detail: The auditor cannot obtain assurance over usable and unusable reserves, with opening balances at 1 April 2025 dependent on completion of work to rebuild assurance over prior years. This creates uncertainty over the council's starting cash position for the year.
findings.matters: Reserve balances determine a council's financial resilience, cash headroom, and ability to absorb economic shocks. A lender cannot assess whether the council has adequate liquidity or can survive a downturn without knowing its reserve position.
findings.figures: Opening reserve balances at 1 April 2025 unquantified; assurance dependent on multi-year rebuild programme
findings.quote: our ability to obtain assurance over the usable and unusable reserves of the Council remains dependent on the completion of our work programme to rebuild assurance following the disclaimed audit opinions.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 for External Audit plan Addendum
findings.headline: £299.6 million of council dwellings (the council's largest asset class) has no audit assurance over valuation or depreciation
findings.detail: The auditor could not obtain assurance over PPE valuations for 2024/25 due to lack of appropriate evidence, and no working papers were provided for depreciation calculations. Council dwellings represent 530% of the council's annual gross expenditure (£56.54 million) but have no audited baseline for comparison.
findings.matters: Unaudited valuations of £299.6 million create material misstatement risk. Valuation assumptions (useful lives, market values, impairment) are subject to significant estimation and could materially overstate or understate the asset base and annual depreciation charges.
findings.figures: £299.6 million council dwellings (31 March 2025); gross annual expenditure £56.54 million
findings.quote: Council dwellings represent a significant balance in the Council's accounts (£299.6 million at 31 March 2025) and are subject to valuation changes, impairment reviews and depreciation charges.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 for External Audit plan Addendum
findings.headline: Three consecutive years of disclaimed audit opinions (2022/23–2024/25) with no assurance expected to rebuild in 2025/26
findings.detail: The council received disclaimed audit opinions for three consecutive years due to failure to produce accounts to planned timetable (2022/23, 2023/24) and inability to provide audit evidence in 2024/25. The auditor explicitly states it is unlikely to commence rebuilding assurance over the historic position in 2025/26, meaning a fourth consecutive year of unqualified opinion is probable.
findings.matters: A lender cannot assess creditworthiness or financial stability without reliable, audited financial statements. Three consecutive disclaimed opinions suggest structural control and reporting deficiencies that are unlikely to be resolved in the near term.
findings.figures: Three consecutive disclaimed opinions (2022/23, 2023/24, 2024/25); no audit procedures completed for 2022/23 and 2023/24; unable to rebuild assurance during 2025/26
findings.quote: However, because we were unable to complete any audit procedures for 2022/23 and 2023/24 and could not complete all planned procedures for 2024/25 for the reasons outlined above, it is unlikely that we will commence any rebuilding of assurance over the historic position during the 2025/26 audit cycle.

findings.headline: £10m PWLB loan and £5m inter-council loan maturing within seven months requiring refinancing
findings.detail: The council has £10m of PWLB debt maturing on 27 March 2027 and £5m of short-term borrowing from another local authority that has been rolled to 17 December 2026. Both require refinancing or repayment. The council is holding this maturity in its debt profile and monitoring rates for optimal refinancing timing.
findings.matters: A lender needs to know about near-term debt maturity, especially amounts that are material relative to the council's size. At current PWLB rates and forecast declines, this is manageable but timing matters.
findings.figures: £10m PWLB maturing 27 March 2027; £5m short-term loan maturing 17 December 2026 (rolled at 4.10% until next maturity)
findings.quote: The Council currently has a £10m PWLB loan maturing on 27 March 2027 and £5m of short-term borrowing from another local authority.

findings.headline: Total capital expenditure running 25% below revised budget at quarter end
findings.detail: Forecast capital expenditure is £40.8m against a revised budget of £54.4m, a £13.6m underspend. The council notes that low spending in Q1 is normal as expenditure typically accelerates later in the year, and majority of projects remain on track for 2026/27 delivery. However, the scale of underspend (£11m on HRA alone, £2.6m on General Fund) is material to monitor.
findings.matters: A lender needs visibility of whether major capital schemes are genuinely on track or whether there are latent delays. Underspends can signal either prudent pacing or delivery risk.
findings.figures: Total forecast £40.8m vs revised budget £54.4m (25% under); HRA £32.6m vs £43.6m; General Fund £8.2m vs £10.8m
findings.quote: Tables 8 and 9 below show relatively low levels of capital expenditure during Q1. However, the current forecast indicates that the majority of planned projects are still expected to be delivered in 2026/27. Progress is now being seen on the Brookfield Close development, and expenditure on the Strategic Housing Delivery Programme is expected to increase as works continue.

findings.headline: Planned HRA borrowing deferred to next financial year due to high rates
findings.detail: The HRA budget included provision to refinance an existing £10m loan and undertake additional borrowing to support capital programmes. However, new borrowing is being deferred until 2027/28 because the council has sufficient cash balances and current PWLB rates remain elevated. This may impact the pace of HRA capital scheme delivery.
findings.matters: A lender needs to know when planned borrowing is not occurring as budgeted, as it signals both the council's risk appetite (deferring at high rates) and potential capital programme delays.
findings.figures: HRA capital forecast £32.6m vs budget £43.6m (£11m reduction, or 25%); planned £10m refinance deferred
findings.quote: The HRA budget included provision to refinance an existing £10m loan and undertake additional borrowing to support the HRA capital programme. However, given the Council's current cash balances and the continuing high level of borrowing rates, it is anticipated that any new borrowing will be deferred until the next financial year.

findings.headline: Three audit recommendations remain overdue with multiple revised implementation dates missed
findings.detail: Three prior audit recommendations (Waste Management, Communications and Information Sharing, Revenues and Benefits Partnership) remain classified as overdue despite progress being made. Multiple revised implementation dates have been missed, with delays linked to Local Government Reorganisation and service reviews.
findings.matters: An s151 officer would need to understand implementation capacity and whether council commitments are being delivered on schedule, particularly when dates are revised multiple times.
findings.figures: 3 overdue; cumulative: 50% completed, 6% in progress, 8% overdue, 36% not yet due
findings.quote: Three recommendations remain overdue. These relate to Waste Management, Communications and Information Sharing, and the Revenues and Benefits Partnership. BDO note that progress is being made in all three areas; however, multiple revised implementation dates have been missed.

findings.headline: Waste service change cannot proceed without £800,000 contribution from Essex County Council
findings.detail: The council pursued a pilot waste scheme and identified a potential service change. The August 2026 report to the Clean and Green Committee confirmed the council cannot conclude or undertake this change without first securing £800,000 from Essex County Council. A decision on proceeding is scheduled for 7 September 2026, after which public consultation would be required.
findings.matters: A lender needs to understand whether planned service improvements depend on securing external funding, and whether the council can reliably obtain it.
findings.figures: £800,000 contribution required
findings.quote: the potential change to the service could not be concluded/ undertaken without firstly securing a £800,000 contribution from Essex County Council towards the change in service; at which point a public consultation will be required

findings.headline: Additional audit fees for assurance rebuilding outside scale fee; 2024/25 variations totalled £48,211
findings.detail: EY's reserve risk assessment and procedures for rebuilding historical assurance are outside the scope of the scale fee and a variation will be sought. Previous year scale fee variations totalled £48,211. Council has budgeted prudently, but if additional fees exceed budget they will be funded from in-year savings or reserves.
findings.matters: If unbudgeted audit costs require reserve drawdown, this further depletes the very reserves the council is trying to protect and rebuild assurance over.
findings.figures: 2024/25 scale fee variations: £48,211
findings.quote: procedures relating to the rebuilding of historical assurance will also be outside the scale fee. Accordingly, we will seek a variation to the scale fee to reflect these changes to the scope of our work and will communicate further through our reporting once the costs are agreed. For context 2024/25 scale fee variations totalled £48,211.

findings.headline: Reserve balances may contain undetected historical misstatements from prior years without complete audit evidence
findings.detail: EY's assessment highlights the possibility that historical misstatements could exist within reserve balances and remain undetected due to absence of complete audit evidence from prior years. The assessment is focused on audit assurance risk rather than evidence of actual financial failure, but the possibility of undetected errors remains.
findings.matters: Lenders assessing reserve strength need to understand this risk; undetected errors would affect the actual available reserves for financial stability.
findings.figures: Historic gaps from four years of disclaimed opinions (2021/22 onwards)
findings.quote: the report highlights the possibility that historical misstatements could exist within reserve balances and remain undetected due to the absence of complete audit evidence from prior years.

findings.headline: Council missed the 2023/24 statutory deadline for accounts publication and is now behind NAO's indicative timeline for audit assurance rebuilding
findings.detail: The NAO's LARRIG 01 guidance assumes audit assurance is obtained during 2023/24 as a starting point for rebuilding. Brentwood's 2023/24 accounts were not published by the statutory deadline, so no audit was undertaken that year. The Council is therefore effectively playing catch-up with the rest of the indicative timetable.
findings.matters: Missing a statutory deadline for accounts publication indicates financial reporting weakness and material delay in rebuilding auditor confidence in financial position.
findings.figures: 2023/24 accounts deadline missed; LARRIG 01 timeline delayed
findings.quote: Brentwood's 2023/24 accounts were not published by the statutory deadline and, as a result, no audit was undertaken for that year. This means the Council did not benefit from the initial assurance assumed within the LARRIG 01 timeline and is therefore effectively playing catch up with the rest of the indicative timetable.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 for Internal audit update Q1
findings.headline: Failed recruitment for policy role is delaying delivery of council-wide data quality framework
findings.detail: A medium-priority Performance Management Framework recommendation requiring a council-wide data quality policy has been extended from April 2026 to September 2026 because recruitment for a Policy and Engagement Specialist post was unsuccessful. The council notes this has 'further impact on delivery of this recommendation' and is seeking additional time for recruitment and training.
findings.matters: A failed recruitment for a key policy role affecting data quality across all services suggests either capacity constraints or difficulty attracting candidates, and delays implementation of governance controls over performance data used for management and reporting.
findings.figures: One vacant Policy and Engagement Specialist post
findings.quote: The Council have undertaken a round of recruitment but been unsuccessful in recruiting to the post of Policy and Engagement Specialist. As such, there has been a further impact on delivery of this recommendation.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 for Internal audit update Q1
findings.headline: Revenues and Benefits partnership contract procedures remain incomplete after multiple missed implementation dates, delayed by Local Government Reorganisation uncertainty
findings.detail: A medium-priority recommendation to establish formal contract change procedures and documentation for the Revenues and Benefits shared service partnership has been pushed from April 2026 to December 2026. The council states the delay is due to Local Government Reorganisation (merger effective 1 April 2028) and uncertainty over future delivery models. Shared service meetings are being documented but formal contract change controls are not yet in place.
findings.matters: Lack of formal contract change procedures in a shared service partnership creates governance risk and makes it unclear how cost or service changes are controlled; combined with reorganisation uncertainty, this suggests the partnership's future terms remain unsettled.
findings.figures: Multiple missed dates: September 2024 → December 2024 → May 2025 → October 2025 → December 2025 → July 2026 → December 2026
findings.quote: The timing of this work has been influenced by the ongoing review of the Revenues and Benefits service, particularly considering Local Government Reorganisation and the potential future delivery models for the service, including the possibility that the current contractual and governance arrangements may change.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 for Internal audit update Q1
findings.headline: High-priority waste management strategy recommendation overdue by two years, pending £800k county contribution and public consultation
findings.detail: The council's waste management strategy — a High priority recommendation due June 2024 — has missed multiple revised deadlines (June 2025, June 2026, now September 2026). A pilot scheme concluded in July 2026 identified that service changes cannot proceed without securing £800,000 contribution from Essex County Council. A further report to Committee on 7 September 2026 will seek a decision on whether to pursue the service change.
findings.matters: A two-year delay on a high-priority operational strategy, combined with a dependency on external funding and decision uncertainty, signals either service cost pressure or capability constraints that could affect service delivery or borrowing requirements.
findings.figures: £800,000 contribution required from Essex County Council
findings.quote: the potential change to the service could not be concluded/ undertaken without firstly securing a £800,000 contribution from Essex County Council towards the change in service; at which point a public consultation will be required before any strategy can be finalised

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for External Audit plan Addendum
findings.headline: Fee variation required; additional costs for risk assessment and historical rebuild work outside scale fee
findings.detail: The risk assessment procedures, MHCLG submission, and addendum drafting are outside the agreed scale fee. Additionally, any procedures relating to rebuilding historical assurance will also be outside scope, requiring a fee variation to be agreed.
findings.matters: Fee variations signal unplanned audit complexity. A lender tracking audit costs sees this as evidence of financial reporting problems escalating beyond normal scope, adding to total costs of audit recovery.
findings.figures: Fee variation to be communicated; outside scale fee set April 2026
findings.quote: the activities undertaken in relation to this risk assessment, the preparation of the submission required by MHCLG, and the drafting of this addendum are outside the scope of the scale fee

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for External Audit plan Addendum
findings.headline: Financial statements contain insufficient quality working papers, lack audit trails, and have unresolved audit queries across significant account areas
findings.detail: The auditors cite 'insufficient quality or unsupported working papers, lack of clear audit trails, unresolved audit queries and evidence gaps across several significant account areas' as a barrier to audit completion. This indicates systemic control and documentation failures, not isolated issues.
findings.matters: Poor working paper quality and unresolved audit queries suggest weak financial controls and record-keeping. This creates risk of undetected error and raises questions about management's commitment to financial governance.
findings.figures: Multiple significant account areas affected
findings.quote: insufficient quality or unsupported working papers, lack of clear audit trails, unresolved audit queries and evidence gaps across several significant account areas

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for External Audit plan Addendum
findings.headline: Auditors will not perform full audit rebuild in 2025/26; council deprioritised despite being in Local Government Reorganisation period
findings.detail: Ernst & Young explicitly states they will not rebuild assurance for Brentwood in 2025/26. They are focusing resources only on councils that 'have demonstrated they are able to adequately support the completion of all 2025/26 planned audit procedures'. Brentwood has been judged unable to meet this threshold. The timeline shows the council is 'behind the expected timescales' for audit recovery.
findings.matters: Active deprioritisation by the external auditor signals the council's financial reporting is not audit-ready. This occurs during Local Government Reorganisation, making the audit position a material governance risk at a time of structural instability.
findings.figures: Deprioritisation for 2025/26; re-assessment planned 2026/27
findings.quote: we will therefore focus our audit resources on rebuilding assurance for those bodies that have demonstrated they are able to adequately support the completion of all 2025/26 planned audit procedures

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for External Audit plan Addendum
findings.headline: Housing Revenue Account (HRA) is separately material and unaudited, with complex statutory interactions creating significant audit risk
findings.detail: The HRA is material and represents cumulative housing landlord income and expenditure. It is statutory ring-fenced but has disclaimed opinions across all four years. The auditors assess it as Significant Risk due to statutory ring-fencing, interaction with capital financing, depreciation and the Major Repairs Reserve.
findings.matters: HRA balances support council housing operations and cannot be mixed with General Fund. An unaudited HRA creates separate hidden risks in a material part of the balance sheet.
findings.figures: HRA balance is material; disclaimed 2021/22, 2022/23, 2023/24, 2024/25
findings.quote: Given the statutory ring-fencing of the HRA, its interaction with capital financing, depreciation and the Major Repairs Reserve, we consider it as significant risk.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for External Audit plan Addendum
findings.headline: General Fund balance is unaudited and material; contains cumulative unidentified misstatements from four years
findings.detail: The General Fund closing balance is assessed as Significant Risk. Assurance has not been obtained over opening balances or movements during the four disclaimed years. The auditors note that 'misstatements arising in the disclaimed years were not identified or corrected and may persist', and turnover in the finance team increases the risk that historical issues were not followed through.
findings.matters: The General Fund is a key indicator of financial resilience. Without audit assurance over this material balance, a lender cannot assess the council's true reserve position or ability to manage budget shocks.
findings.figures: General Fund balance is material; four disclaimed audit years: 2021/22–2024/25
findings.quote: Assurance has therefore not been obtained over the General Fund opening balance or all movements during the disclaimed period. There remains an increased risk that misstatements arising in the disclaimed years were not identified or corrected and may persist in the opening balance for the current audit year.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for External Audit plan Addendum
findings.headline: Four consecutive years of disclaimed audit opinions mean no audited financial statements exist for 2021/22–2024/25
findings.detail: The audits for 2021/22, 2022/23, 2023/24 and 2024/25 were all disclaimed, meaning Ernst & Young could not form any opinion on the financial statements. Even planned procedures for 2024/25 were not completed. This represents a total loss of audit assurance over cumulative balances and reserves spanning four years.
findings.matters: A lender cannot assess actual financial position without audited accounts. Brentwood's inability to produce auditable financial statements for four years is a fundamental governance and control failure.
findings.quote: the audits for 2021/22, 2022/23, 2023/24 and 2024/25 were disclaimed, and not all planned procedures were completed for 2024/25

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Brentwood Borough Council Provisional audit planning report Year ending 31 March 2026
findings.headline: Audit completion depends on the council meeting agreed timelines for evidence provision and responding promptly to audit queries
findings.detail: Auditors explicitly state: 'Our ability to complete the audit is dependent on the timely formulation of appropriately supported accounting judgements, provision of accurate and relevant supporting evidence, access to the finance team and management's responsiveness to issues identified during the audit.' An agreed timetable has been established, with compliance being 'essential.'
findings.matters: The audit's successful completion — and thus issuance of an opinion — is contingent on management delivering on multiple commitments. Given prior delays and quality issues, there is risk the council may not meet these obligations, delaying the audit further.
findings.figures: Audit Results Report due December 2026; Auditor's Annual Report due before 30 November 2026
findings.quote: Our ability to complete the audit is dependent on the timely formulation of appropriately supported accounting judgements, provision of accurate and relevant supporting evidence, access to the finance team and management's responsiveness to issues identified during the audit. An audit timetable has been agreed with management. In Section 7 we include a provisional timeline for the audit. It is essential that all parties collaborate to ensure compliance with this timeline.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Brentwood Borough Council Provisional audit planning report Year ending 31 March 2026
findings.headline: New accounting standard (CIPFA Bulletin 22) on asset valuation to be implemented for 2025/26, requiring quinquennial revaluations or five-year rolling programmes
findings.detail: The council will be required to apply CIPFA Bulletin 22 in 2025/26, which mandates either a quinquennial revaluation or a five-year rolling programme for formal valuations of non-investment assets, with annual indexation in intervening years. Auditors note they are 'liaising with management to understand their application' and will assess impact on risks once the approach is established.
findings.matters: Implementation of new valuation standards can affect asset valuations materially and requires robust processes to ensure compliance. Given the council's prior issues with PPE valuation evidence and quality, successful implementation is uncertain and represents a risk to financial statement reliability.
findings.figures: Requirement: quinquennial revaluation or five-year rolling programme with annual indexation; applies to non-investment assets (PPE, surplus, community assets)
findings.quote: Additionally, in the 2025/26 financial statements the Council will be required to apply CIPFA Bulletin 22 which reassesses the current regime of valuation for non-investment assets across the public sector. The guidance mandates a quinquennial revaluation or a five-year rolling programme for formal valuations, supported by annual indexation in the intervening years.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Brentwood Borough Council Provisional audit planning report Year ending 31 March 2026
findings.headline: Limited assurance is expected for opening balances in 2025/26 and closing reserves, due to gaps in prior-year audit work
findings.detail: Auditors anticipate having limited assurance over opening balances for 2025/26 and limited assurance over the closing reserves balance due to uncertainty over the opening amount. This stems from the inability to complete audit procedures in prior years when disclaimers were issued.
findings.matters: Limited assurance on reserves means the council's reported financial position and available resources cannot be fully verified. For a lender, this creates uncertainty about the council's true financial standing and liquidity position.
findings.figures: Opening balances 2025/26: limited assurance anticipated; closing reserves 2025/26: limited assurance anticipated
findings.quote: We will have limited assurance over the opening balances for 2025/26; and Limited assurance over the closing reserves balance, due to uncertainty over the opening amount.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Brentwood Borough Council Provisional audit planning report Year ending 31 March 2026
findings.headline: Audit materiality reduced to reflect elevated risk from disclaimed opinions and prior misstatements
findings.detail: Performance materiality (the threshold for audit procedures) has been set at £0.51m, representing 50% of group materiality of £1.02m. Auditors note this lower figure reflects 'increased risk of material misstatements considering historical disclaimed audit opinions and the misstatements identified in 2024/25.' This means auditors are treating the council as higher-risk.
findings.matters: Lower materiality thresholds indicate auditors consider the council a higher-risk audit engagement due to past opinion failures and misstatements. This signals increased audit risk and reduced confidence in management's accounting processes.
findings.figures: Group materiality £1.02m (1.8% of 2024/25 gross expenditure); performance materiality £0.51m (50% of planning materiality)
findings.quote: Group Performance materiality has been set at £0.51 million, which represents 50% of materiality... This reflects the increased risk of material misstatements considering historical disclaimed audit opinions and the misstatements identified in 2024/25.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Brentwood Borough Council Provisional audit planning report Year ending 31 March 2026
findings.headline: The council's Minimum Revenue Provision (MRP) calculation has not been audited since 2020/21, when a fraud risk was identified
findings.detail: Auditors identified MRP as an inherent risk because they have not audited this balance since 2020/21, when they identified a fraud risk due to the council's increased financing and level of judgement in the calculation. Historical work found errors requiring adjustment, though concluded these were not fraudulent. This will be re-examined in 2025/26.
findings.matters: MRP is a mandatory charge to the General Fund each year based on the Capital Financing Requirement. Errors or inappropriate calculation can misstate revenue expenditure and the General Fund balance, affecting the council's reported financial position and borrowing decisions.
findings.figures: Last audited 2020/21; identified as inherent risk with previously identified errors in calculation
findings.quote: We identified a fraud risk in relation to MRP in 2020/21, due to the Council's increase in financing and the level of judgement applied in the determining the basis of the calculation. We undertook procedures in 2020/21 to check the MRP calculation which resulted in proposed adjustments to the calculation and recommendations which were shared with Management.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Brentwood Borough Council Provisional audit planning report Year ending 31 March 2026
findings.headline: No assurance could be obtained on Property, Plant and Equipment valuation due to lack of evidence, and working papers for depreciation were not provided
findings.detail: The council's auditors state they obtained no assurance on PPE valuation for the 2024/25 audit due to insufficient evidence and lack of supporting working papers on asset depreciation. Council dwellings alone are valued at £299.57 million, making this a material balance sheet item.
findings.matters: PPE represents a significant portion of the council's asset base. Without audit assurance on valuations or depreciation, the council's reported asset values cannot be verified, affecting balance sheet reliability and any asset-backed borrowing decisions.
findings.figures: Council dwellings valued at £299.57 million; land and buildings at £82.45 million; investment properties £23.28 million (Council) and £56.73 million (subsidiary SAIL)
findings.quote: No assurance was obtained on the Property, Plant and Equipment (PPE) of the Council with respect to the valuation of assets due to the lack of appropriate and sufficient evidence for the 2024/25 audit. In addition, no working papers were provided by management in relation to the depreciation of the Council's assets for the 2024/25 audit.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 1 for Brentwood Borough Council Provisional audit planning report Year ending 31 March 2026
findings.headline: The council has received disclaimed audit opinions for two consecutive years and is behind the expected timeline for rebuilding assurance
findings.detail: Brentwood received disclaimers of opinion for the years ended 31 March 2024 and 2025 due to failure to produce accounts in accordance with its planned timetable. The auditor notes the council's recovery is behind the expected timescales set out in National Audit Office guidance, and unlikely to commence rebuilding assurance over the historic position during 2025/26.
findings.matters: Disclaimed opinions indicate the auditor could not form any opinion on whether the financial statements are reliable, which is a critical red flag for any lender assessing creditworthiness and the council's financial control environment.
findings.figures: Disclaimer opinions issued 2023/24 and 2024/25; no assurance procedures completed for 2022/23 or 2023/24
findings.quote: In the audit reports for the years ended 31 March 2024 and 31 March 2025, a disclaimer of opinion was issued due to the application of the backstop. This means the auditor has not been able to form an opinion on the financial statements.

findings.headline: Medium-term financial sustainability is challenged by multiple concurrent structural pressures including Local Government Reorganisation.
findings.detail: The Council's Medium-Term Financial Strategy identifies a challenging financial environment from funding reform, business rates reset, inflationary pressures, demand pressures, audit recovery requirements and Local Government Reorganisation (LGR). These concurrent pressures create risks to medium-term sustainability that must be managed through robust budgeting and adequate reserves.
findings.matters: Lenders assess debt capacity based on medium-term financial sustainability; multiple structural pressures reduce financial headroom and increase refinancing risk.
findings.figures: No specific deficits or reserve impacts disclosed
findings.quote: The Council's Medium-Term Financial Strategy identifies a challenging financial environment. Funding reform, business rates reset, inflationary pressures, demand pressures, recovery of audit assurance and Local Government Reorganisation all create risks to medium-term financial sustainability.

findings.headline: Procurement controls are not yet consistently applied in practice across services despite established procedures.
findings.detail: The council has established structured procurement arrangements and uses the Essex Procurement Partnership, but audit findings confirm controls remain inconsistently embedded. Further work is required to ensure procurement is consistently planned, documented, monitored and supported by clear audit trails.
findings.matters: Inconsistent procurement controls indicate governance weakness that could lead to contract compliance failures and uncontrolled spend.
findings.figures: No specific figures
findings.quote: However, audit findings and follow-up reporting confirm that, despite these arrangements, controls are not yet consistently embedded in practice across all services.

findings.headline: Local authority company has unresolved legal and financial matters requiring ongoing oversight and creating financial exposure.
findings.detail: The council has strengthened governance over its local authority company but significant matters remain unresolved. The statement references engagement with external legal advisors for 'company-related matters and disputes' and explicitly flags the need for continued close oversight of financial exposure, legal risk, settlement considerations and future company strategy.
findings.matters: Unresolved company disputes and financial exposure could create contingent liabilities affecting the council's balance sheet and debt capacity.
findings.figures: No financial figures disclosed
findings.quote: While progress has been made, this remains a key governance area and will continue to require close oversight, particularly in relation to financial exposure, legal risk, settlement considerations and future company strategy.

findings.headline: Finance team capacity is insufficient to manage accounts closedown and audit support, affecting audit recovery.
findings.detail: The audit process highlighted that finance capacity is both an operational and governance issue. The council recognises that audit recovery depends on sufficient team capacity, clear coordination, disciplined working paper preparation and timely responses to audit queries. A capacity review is scheduled for 2026/27.
findings.matters: Insufficient capacity to produce reliable accounts and support the audit process represents a material control weakness affecting financial reporting credibility.
findings.figures: No specific numbers provided
findings.quote: The audit process also highlighted the importance of finance team capacity to prepare the accounts and support the audit process.

findings.headline: External audit report for 2024/25 was disclaimed, with specific accounting issues preventing sign-off.
findings.detail: The council received a disclaimed audit opinion for 2024/25, reflecting the national audit reset. Specific audit issues identified include problems with prior year adjustments, statement presentation, balance sheet classification, cash and cash equivalents, overdraft presentation, group accounts, leases and account classifications. The council must rebuild audit assurance through improved financial reporting, evidence, reconciliations and working papers.
findings.matters: A disclaimed opinion means financial statements are unassured; lenders cannot rely on reported figures to assess creditworthiness until assurance is restored.
findings.figures: 2024/25 audit report disclaimed
findings.quote: The audit report for Brentwood's 2024/25 accounts was disclaimed.

findings.headline: Investment income outperformed budget by £3.490m due to favourable interest rates
findings.detail: The council achieved £7.137m in investment returns against a budget of £3.647m, a 96% outperformance. The £3.490m windfall was transferred to earmarked reserves. This reflects 'favourable market rates and strong cash balances' as the Bank of England cut rates from 4.50% to 3.75% during the year. The council holds £142.428m invested across 18 other UK local authorities.
findings.matters: While positive, this exceptional return reflects falling interest rates and should not be assumed sustainable; finance directors need to ensure this one-time boost does not fund recurring spending commitments.
findings.figures: Investment income £7.137m vs budget £3.647m. Surplus £3.490m transferred to reserves. Total investments £142.428m.
findings.quote: Investment income achieved during the year was £7.137m compared with a budget of £3.647m generating an additional £3.490m of income for the Council which has been transferred to earmarked reserves.

findings.headline: Council avoided external borrowing despite £205.766m capital financing requirement
findings.detail: The capital programme was entirely funded from internal sources: £5.1m from capital receipts, £6.121m from grants, £3.084m from reserves, and £3.815m from internal cash resources. The council 'did not undertake any external borrowing' despite material financing need, choosing instead to 'avoid the need to borrow at a time when borrowing costs remained elevated'.
findings.matters: The decision to preserve borrowing capacity while rates are high is prudent but means the council has limited new debt headroom and is managing within existing resources; future capital programmes may face greater constraints.
findings.figures: Capital expenditure £18.120m funded entirely from internal sources. External borrowing £0m for 2025/26.
findings.quote: The Council did not undertake any external borrowing. Capital expenditure was financed through a combination of capital receipts, grants, revenue contributions, reserves and internal cash resources. This approach avoided the need to borrow at a time when borrowing costs remained elevated

findings.headline: Financing costs increased to 36.80% of net revenue in 2025/26, up sharply from 20% prior year
findings.detail: The Ratio of Financing Costs to Net Revenue Stream jumped from 20.00% in 2024/25 to 36.80% in 2025/26 – an 84% increase. This reflects the council's £205.766m Capital Financing Requirement and shows more than one-third of all revenue is now committed to servicing past capital expenditure. The council budgeted for an even higher 43.50% but came in below.
findings.matters: The sharp increase in financing cost ratio constrains financial flexibility and signals rising debt burden relative to income; this leaves less room to absorb new pressures or invest in services.
findings.quote: Ratio of Financing Costs to Net Revenue Stream 20.00% 43.50% 36.80%

findings.headline: Capital programme delivered £18.1m of £28.1m budget, leaving £9.978m underspent and delayed
findings.detail: The approved capital expenditure budget of £28.098m resulted in actual spending of only £18.120m, an underspend of £9.978m (35%). The largest shortfall was in 'A Place to call home' (housing and social housing development) which underspent by £6.388m. The report attributes this to 'timing of project delivery rather than cancellation' but does not explain which schemes have slipped or their new delivery dates.
findings.matters: Significant capital slippage indicates project delivery risk and changes when funding will be drawn; lenders need clarity on whether schemes are stalled or merely delayed, and when the £9.978m will be spent.
findings.figures: Budget £28.098m, Outturn £18.120m, Underspend £9.978m. 'A Place to call home' underspent £6.388m.
findings.quote: The variance largely reflects the timing of project delivery rather than cancellation of approved schemes.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A- HRA & General Fund Capital Outturn
findings.headline: Baytree Public Realm project 99% unspent — only £31k of £3.75m spent
findings.detail: The Baytree Public Realm scheme was budgeted at £3.75m but only £31k was actually spent. This is the second-largest underspend as a single item and suggests a major capital project has stalled entirely, with no meaningful progress in the financial year.
findings.matters: A £3.75m scheme with only £31k spent indicates a major project is either not progressing or has encountered blocking issues (planning, land assembly, scope changes). For a lender, this signals either incomplete planning or external dependencies that the council cannot control, and demonstrates poor project delivery.
findings.figures: Baytree - Public Realm: £3,750k budgeted, £31k spent, £3,719k underspent
findings.quote: Baytree - Public Realm 3,750 31 (3,719)
